format.title: The campaign file format
format.intro: A prepared campaign or adventure fits in a JSON file. A campaign's export writes one; you can also write it by hand, or have a tool write it, following this page. At creation, “Import” reads it, checks every field and says exactly what is wrong.
format.twoFilesIntro: The “format” field says which one it is.
format.campaignFile: a whole campaign: its settings, adventures, codex and quests. It creates a new campaign.
format.adventureFile: a single adventure, to add to an existing campaign (“New adventure” › Import).
format.notIncluded: Only the preparation travels: never members, characters, played sessions, recaps, journals or the GM's notebook. Everything arrives hidden: codex entries and quests are revealed later, in play.
format.strict: An unknown field is an error, not something silently dropped. Fields followed by “?” are optional. Locations are named: an enemy or an NPC quotes the “name” of a location of the same adventure.
format.exampleIntro: “Les Brumes d'Ashmoor”, a small invented campaign. An adventure file holds “format”, “packs” and a single “adventure”.

campaign.name: The campaign's name.
campaign.characterSystem: The kind of sheet: “5e” (computed 5E sheet) or “standard” (free sheet).

adventure.title: The title.
adventure.summary: The summary, a reminder for the GM.

location.name: The name, unique within the adventure.
location.imageUrl: The map or illustration, as a link (https://…).
location.hidden: true: the location shows under the fog, to uncover with the brush.
location.loot: The hidden loot: { items?: [{ name, quantity? }], money?: { platinum?, gold?, electrum?, silver?, copper? } }.

enemy.name: The name.
enemy.speed: The speed in metres (9 by default).
enemy.location: The name of one of the adventure's locations.
enemy.sourceMonsterId: The id of an SRD or pack monster (“goblin”).
enemy.attacks: The attacks: { name, toHit?, reach?, damage?: { count, die }, damageBonus?, damageKind?, notes? }.
enemy.loot: The loot it carries, to give once it falls: { items?: [{ name, quantity? }], money?: { platinum?, gold?, electrum?, silver?, copper? } }.

npc.name: The name.
npc.personality: Their temper in a few words.
npc.location: The name of one of the adventure's locations.

event.title: The title.
event.description: What happens, as the players will read it.
event.trigger: What sets it off (“when they enter the crypt”).
event.dueDay: The game day it is due (“Day 3”: 3).
event.dueTime: The game time it is due (“22:00”). With or without a day: the GM's panel says “it's time” when the clock gets there.

codex.name: The name.
codex.summary: What the players will learn once revealed (Markdown, [[Name]] mentions).
codex.url: A document hosted elsewhere, as a link.
codex.reputation: For a faction: its attitude toward the party, from −3 to 3.

pack.name: Its name, for the message when the pack is missing.

prompt.campaign:
Help me prepare a tabletop role-playing campaign for the Adventure Keeper app. I am attaching an example file in the "{{format}}" format. Write a complete campaign file in the same format, from my description or the document I attach: campaign settings, adventures (locations, enemies, NPCs, story beats), codex and quests.

Rules:
- Reply with the JSON only, valid, with no comment or text around it.
- Keep "format" as "{{format}}" and the same structure as the example.
- Add no field the example does not have: an unknown field makes the import fail.
- An enemy or NPC names a location by its "name", which must exist in the same adventure.

My campaign:
